  unit-testable without a live session store) resolves model and level independently: an explicit flag
  always wins for its own half; otherwise `Persistence::model_and_level_at_active` — the same lookup
  `switch_session` uses — supplies the reattached session's own last-recorded value, which already falls
  back to `cfg.model`/the CLI-resolved level itself when nothing was ever recorded (a genuinely fresh
  session, or pure in-memory mode), so this is a no-op there.
- **`run` resumes on the session's model, over that model's route** — `run` selects its session
  (`RunSession`) right after resolving `--model`, before anything model-keyed: the credential and
  route (`resolve_gateway_credential_and_headers`, including a `models.json` `base_url`/`headers`),
  vision, the reasoning default and the context window. Existing sessions are opened there; a fresh one
  is only selected and is created once every check has passed (`SessionRepo::resume_latest` /
  `open_id_if_exists` are the create-free halves of `resume_latest_or_create` / `open_or_create_id`).
  Without an explicit `--model`, the model is the resumed session's active one: `model_at` its tip,
  else its creation model, the same lookup as `model_and_level_at_active`. An explicit `--model` that
  differs is recorded with `record_model_change`, so `a → --continue --model b → --continue` stays on
  `b`. Before this, the credential was resolved for the CLI default and the session's model was sent
  over it, and a switch was never recorded, so the next `--continue` reverted to the creation model.
- **Reopening closes a prompt a killed process never answered** — the prompt is checkpointed before
  the model call, so a process killed outright (OOM, `kill -9`, a deploy's SIGKILL) leaves a session
  whose tip is that `user` message (or a tool-results turn) with no closing record: no `Err` path ran
  to write one. Every host that reopens a session calls `serve::close_interrupted_prompt` before
  adding its own prompt — `run` on resume, `serve` on open (stdio, daemon, service) and on
  `switch_session` — which appends the same synthetic `Message::error` record a failed run leaves
  ("interrupted: the previous run ended before answering this request"), so the request never carries
  `[user, user]` and the model is told the earlier request was cut off. Held only in memory until the
  next write persists it. A `serve` host bash record (`serve::is_host_bash_record`) is a `user` message
  that legitimately ends a session between prompts, so it is left alone. `switch_branch` is not a
  reopen: navigating to a `user` entry is deliberate.
- **Reset to root** — `switch_branch`'s `before: bool` (mirroring `fork`'s identical flag) switches to
  `target_id`'s own _parent_ instead of `target_id` itself; when `target_id` is the very first message,
  its parent is the tree's own root (before any message), which is exactly "redo the first message in
  place" — pi's own `SessionManager::resetLeaf`. No separate root sentinel exists on the wire: the
  client already has real entry ids from `get_fork_messages`, so `{target_id: <first message>,
  before: true}` means precisely that. `SessionStore::switch_active_to_root`/
  `switch_active_to_root_with_summary`/`abandoned_to_root` are the root-specific counterparts of
  `switch_active`/`switch_active_with_summary`/`abandoned_by_switch`; `Entry::Leaf.target_id` is
  `Option<String>` (`None` = root) so the reset survives a reopen — a legacy file's own bare-string
  `target_id` still deserializes as `Some(..)`, no migration needed. Model/thinking-level restoration
  for a `before`-resolved switch queries the _resolved_ target (`Persistence::model_and_level_at_opt`,
  reading `SessionStore::model_at_root`/`thinking_level_at_root` for the root case), not the raw,
  pre-resolution `target_id` argument — those two can disagree whenever a change is anchored exactly at
  the resolved parent, since an anchored change takes effect for what comes _after_ that point, not the
  point itself.
- **Expanded `serve` surface** — beyond `prompt`/`get_state`/`get_messages`/`new_session`: `abort`,
  `stop_after_turn` (graceful — the current turn's tool calls still finish and commit; only the _next_
  model call is skipped — see `agent_core::Steering::request_stop`), `steer` (mid-run, folded onto the
  next tool turn) / `follow_up` (queued for the next stop boundary, and — unlike a bare
  `steer`/`follow_up` — also accepted while idle, queuing against a persistent handle for whichever
  `prompt` runs next; `stop_after_turn` sent while idle is instead a no-op ack, since there is no future
  run it could safely bind to). Every path that queues a raw user-authored message this way — `steer`,
  `follow_up` (both the idle and mid-run handlers), and `prompt`'s `streaming_behavior:"steer"|"follow_up"`
  variant — expands a `/skill:name`/`/name` invocation exactly like a fresh `prompt` does (`serve.rs`'s
  shared `expand_message` helper) and accepts the same optional `images` array a fresh `prompt` does
  (parsed via `parse_images` into an `agent_core::SteeringMessage`), so neither expansion nor image
  attachments are a `prompt`-only behavior a client has to special-case. **Each steering lane is
  bounded** (`agent_core::steering`'s per-lane cap): the lanes are fed straight from remote RPC, carry
  base64 image payloads, and drain at most one message per turn boundary — and the steer lane has no
  drain point at all while idle — so an unbounded lane lets one client pin arbitrary heap in the daemon
  for the session's life. A full lane **refuses the newest** message (rather than dropping the oldest,
  which would silently reorder the client's own instruction stream and, under a sustained flood, churn
  the head so nothing ever reaches the model), and the refusal is reported honestly: the ack comes back
  `success: false` with a `steering queue full` error, alongside the usual `queue_content` payload so
  the client can see the depth it's up against and retry once the agent drains. Acking `true` for a
  message that was dropped is the one outcome a client cannot recover from, since it has no other signal
  that its instruction never reached the model. `compact`(optional `custom_instructions` steers what the summary
  emphasizes, passed straight through to `Agent::compact` — matching pi's own `compact(customInstructions)`;
  response is `{compacted, reason, summary, tokens_before, tokens_after}` — all four of the latter `null`
  on a no-op, or a real compaction's own generated summary text and its `AgentEvent::Compacted`-carried
  before/after token estimates otherwise, matching pi's own `CompactionResult` shape rather than the bare
  `{compacted: bool}` this used to return; `reason` (Task #26 pi-parity fix) is `agent_core::CompactOutcome`'s
  own `"too_small"`/`"already_compacted"` discriminator when `compacted` is `false` — `Agent::compact`
  itself returns a `CompactOutcome` rather than a bare `bool` for exactly this, matching pi's own two
  distinct thrown errors ("Nothing to compact (session too small)" / "Already compacted") instead of
  collapsing both into the same undifferentiated no-op),
  `list_sessions`/`list_all_sessions`(cross-project — every project's own session directory under the
  shared root, not just this one's; each streams unsolicited `list_progress` frames, correlated to the
  request's own `id`, while its parallel scan is in flight — throttled to roughly ten frames regardless
  of how many sessions exist, deterministically by `scanned`'s value so it stays stable despite the
  concurrent scan)/`switch_session`/`delete_session`(soft-delete-to-`.trash`, idempotent; refuses the
  currently active session rather than moving its file out from under the in-memory `Session` a client
  is still using — no RPC surface reached `SessionRepo::delete` before this)/`list_trash`(repo mode;
  `{trash: [{id, deleted_at, original_path}...]}`, most-recently-deleted first — `.trash/` has always
  existed as `delete_session`'s soft-delete destination, but nothing previously read, listed, restored
  from, or pruned it)/`restore_session`(move a trashed session back to its original location; fails
  clearly, not a silent overwrite, if something already occupies that path; reports failure, not
  idempotent success like `delete_session`, when the id isn't in `.trash/` at all — both kept
  deliberately minimal, a low-priority nice-to-have rather than a full trash-management UI); both
  `delete_session`/`switch_session`, along with `fork`'s
  own `target_id` and `--fork`'s CLI resolution, accept a `session_id` that's either a full id or a
  _unique_ prefix of one — `SessionRepo::find_path` tries an exact match first, then a prefix scan; an
  ambiguous prefix (matching more than one session) is an error naming every candidate rather than pi's
  own `resolveSessionPath`, which silently picks whichever sorts first — acting on the wrong session with
  no warning is a real footgun this crate declines to imitate)/`fork`/`clone`(pi's own
  name for a bare `fork` — no `upto`/`target_id` — kept as a thin alias, not a second code path, since
  this crate's `fork` already defaults to the same behavior pi needs `clone` for)/`get_fork_messages`
  (pi's own contract exactly: no parameters, current session only, `{entry_id, text}` per user-turn
  entry anywhere in the tree — every branch, not just the active path, matching pi's own
  `getUserMessagesForForking`/`getEntries()` (every entry ever appended, tree-wide) rather than only the
  active-path chain (`session_store::SessionStore::all_user_messages`) — a candidate list for a client's
  own fork-point picker, feeding one `entry_id` to `fork`'s `target_id`; previously misnamed onto this
  crate's own arbitrary-session/arbitrary-point _preview_ feature instead, breaking a pi-compatible
  client's zero-arg call — that feature now lives at `preview_fork`, unchanged otherwise)/`preview_fork`
  (read-only fork
  preview, any session/point, this crate's own extension beyond pi's protocol)/`set_session_name`(an O(1) `Entry::TitleChange` append, not a rewrite of the whole
  file — a rename used to cost rewriting every message already on disk just to update the header's
  `title` field; whole-session-scoped rather than branch-scoped like `ModelChange`/
  `ThinkingLevelChange`, so the most recent rename anywhere in the file wins regardless of which
  branch is active, matching pi's own `session_info` entries; the title is sanitized first — any run of
  `\r`/`\n` collapses to a single space and the result is trimmed, matching pi's `appendSessionInfo` —
  and a title that sanitizes to empty explicitly clears the stored title rather than persisting a blank
  string)/`export_html`(render the active session's transcript as one
  self-contained HTML file, no server involved once written — plus every abandoned branch
  (`SessionStore::abandoned_branches`), each inline as a collapsible `<details>` block positioned
  right after the message it actually diverged from (native HTML, no client-side JS — the one
  interactive piece the export's otherwise-static-page design makes room for), rendering only the
  part that diverges from the active path so the shared prefix isn't duplicated),
  `get_last_assistant_text`/`get_session_stats`/`get_commands`(+ collision diagnostics; each prompt
  template's `description` field is its own `description:` frontmatter — a one-line summary always
  populated for display — not `argument_hint`, the separate `<file>`-style hint for what to type after
  the name; each skill's `name` is prefixed `skill:` — matching pi's own `get_commands` shape — so the
  listed `name` is always exactly what a client appends after `/` to invoke it, a skill needing the
  `skill:` prefix and a prompt template not; each entry also carries `scope` (`"user"`/`"project"`/
  `"temporary"` — which discovery root it actually came from) and `path` (its on-disk location) — Task
  #39 pi-parity fix, matching pi's own `sourceInfo.scope`/`sourceInfo.path`, previously omitted entirely.
  `skills::Skill`/`prompts::PromptTemplate` are tagged with their own `scope`/`path` once per
  discovery-root group in each module's `discover_with_diagnostics_impl` — `path_utils::
  push_unique_scoped_root` (generalized from the prior `push_unique_root`, which had no callers left
  once both modules needed to carry a scope tag alongside each root) threads the tag through the same
  root-list/dedup structure both already built)/`reload`,
  `set_model`/`set_thinking`(raw budget override)/`set_reasoning_effort`(the portable
  `agent_core::ThinkingLevel`, correct for whichever mechanism the active model actually
  uses)/`cycle_model`(steps through `--models`'s scoped list when given — comma-separated patterns
  resolved by `resolve_model_scope`: a literal id kept verbatim, a glob (`*`/`?`/`[`) expanded
  case-insensitively against `available_models()`, either optionally suffixed `:<thinking-level>` to pin
  that entry's depth for as long as cycling stays on it — else the full known-model hint list; reports
  `scoped: bool` so a client knows which; `set_model` is unaffected either way, accepting any id;
  both `set_model`/`cycle_model` echo back the same `model_info` capability shape
  `get_available_models`' own entries carry — context window, max output, reasoning/vision support —
  so a client doesn't need a separate round trip just to learn the new model's capabilities)/
  `get_available_models`(always the full shown-model list, `serve::listed_models`: the hint list, then
  every chat model in the provider catalog that a native provider serves under its bare id, which
  `list-models` prints too and a test holds to the catalog; partial ids still resolve against the short
  hint list alone, so `--model haiku` stays unambiguous; _never_ narrowed by `--models` — that
  flag only scopes `cycle_model`'s own candidate list; a client's model picker needs the full catalog to
  offer a "show everything" view the way pi's own `/model` selector can Tab out of its scope-defaulted
  view)/
  `cycle_thinking_level`(advances the same portable level)/`set_auto_compaction`/
  `set_auto_retry`(toggle `agent_core::Agent::with_auto_retry` — off surfaces an otherwise-retried
  mid-stream failure on the first attempt, for debugging a flaky connection)
  (rebuild the `Agent` for subsequent prompts) / `get_available_models`, `list_branches`/`get_tree`/`switch_branch`
  (navigate the session's tree, optionally summarizing the abandoned branch first — a summarization
  failure other than a client-requested abort (`Error::Cancelled`) fails the whole switch rather than
  logging it and switching anyway, matching pi's own `packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`'s
  `navigateTree`, which `throw`s on any non-abort summarization error (backed by `generateBranchSummary`
  in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/branch-summarization.ts`), aborting the whole navigation
  before ever switching the active leaf; `get_messages` tags
  each message with its tree `id` so a client can name any point as a `switch_branch` target, not only a
  branch's leaf, and its response also carries `leaf_id` — the same active-tip id `get_tree`'s own
  response already does, matching pi's own `get_entries({since})` returning `{entries, leafId}` in one
  round trip so a client doesn't need a second `get_tree` call just to learn the current tip;
  `get_messages`'s optional `since` — a tree id the client already has — returns only
  what was appended after it, pi's own `get_entries({since})`, so a polling client doesn't have to
  re-transfer the whole transcript every time; an unmatched `since` is an error, not a silent full
  re-fetch), and `bash`/`abort_bash` (run a host shell command directly, independent of the
  model's own tool loop). A `prompt` emits an immediate `ack` frame the moment it's queued, and its
  terminal `response` reports `refused: bool` (a refusal is a distinct terminal condition — it doesn't
  drain queued steering); a `prompt` sent while another is in flight can carry
  `streaming_behavior: "steer"|"follow_up"` to be accepted and queued instead of rejected as busy. A
  `prompt` runs concurrently with stdin so `abort`/`stop_after_turn`/`steer`/`follow_up` land mid-turn.
  A mid-run `abort`'s own success ack is deliberately _not_ sent the instant the cancellation is
  requested — it's held until the cancelled run has actually finished unwinding (the same busy-loop
  keeps rejecting every other command as busy until then), matching pi's own `agent-session.ts` awaiting
  `waitForIdle()` first; sending it earlier let a client that treats the ack as "safe to send the next
  command" (a reasonable reading of the contract) get rejected as busy in the gap.
- **Whole-run auto-retry** — once `agent_core`'s own mid-stream retry (inside one model turn) is
  exhausted, a `prompt` that still ends in a transient-looking `Err`
  (`retry::is_retryable_whole_run` — a superset of `agent_core::agent::is_retryable_mid_stream`, plus
  reqwest's pre-response send failure (`error sending request for url`, which outlasted `client.rs`'s
  own connect retries), plus raw HTTP status-code digits ("429"/"500"/"502"/"503"/"504"/"524") that
  classifier deliberately excludes at
  its own layer: a mid-stream message's "500" is more likely an unrelated number than a real status
  code, but an error reaching this outer layer already exhausted every narrower, more precise check —
  matches pi's own broader net, which is pi's _only_ layer for a plain HTTP-status failure since SDK
  retry is disabled there) is automatically re-invoked against the _same_ session — resuming from
  wherever it left off, not restarting the turn or re-appending the user message — up to 3 more times
  with exponential backoff (2/4/8s, capped at 30s; pi's `agent-session.ts` equivalent; the policy
  constants/backoff/classifier function live in [`retry`](src/retry.rs), shared rather than
  duplicated). Gated by the same `current_auto_retry`/`set_auto_retry` flag as the mid-stream layer (one
  user-facing "retries on/off" concept spanning two internal layers); never retries past a client
  disconnect or an explicit `abort` (redundant with `is_retryable_whole_run` already excluding
  `Error::Cancelled` transitively, but checked explicitly too). Each attempt persists whatever it
  produced (even a failed one may have committed a
  tool round-trip before erroring) before deciding whether to retry — but the retry decision is made
  _first_, and when a retry is coming the attempt's closing error record is withheld from that persist
  and held aside, because `SessionStore::append_new` is keyed on a message **count** and so cannot
  observe the list getting shorter. Persisting the record and only then popping it in memory desynced
  the two permanently: the retry re-produced the assistant message, `len` was back to what had already
  been persisted, the append early-returned, and the recovered turn was never written at all — with the
  following `tool_result` chaining onto the error record's node instead. If the retry is then cancelled
  during its backoff, the withheld record is pushed back and re-persisted (a plain append), since it is
  the only thing keeping role alternation valid for the next `prompt`. Each attempt also emits an
  unsolicited
  `auto_retry_start` frame (matching pi's own wire discriminator — this crate previously emitted a bare
  `auto_retry`) just before its backoff sleep so a client can distinguish "still working, retrying
  a hiccup" from silence. The backoff sleep _is_ raced — against `abort`/`abort_retry`/shutdown, via a
  dedicated inner `select!` scoped to the wait itself (no run is in flight during backoff, so it
  accepts only those two commands plus stdin closing; anything else is rejected as busy) — so a client
  cancelling a pending retry takes effect immediately rather than after the full 2–30s delay elapses.
  A cancelled retry surfaces the _real_ error that triggered it, not a synthetic `Error::Cancelled` —
  nothing was actually cancelled mid-flight, the automatic retry was just declined. A retry sequence
  that made at least one attempt ends with exactly one unsolicited `auto_retry_end` frame — `success`
  when a retried attempt recovers, or `success:false` (with `final_error`) when retries exhaust, the
  failure turns out non-retryable, or the pending backoff is itself cancelled
  (`final_error:"retry cancelled"`) — mirroring pi's own `auto_retry_end` event; never sent for a
  first-attempt success or an immediately-non-retryable failure, which never emitted `auto_retry_start` to
  begin with. `main.rs`'s
  one-shot `run`/`run --json` share the same [`retry`](src/retry.rs) policy (`run_turn`,
  unconditionally on — a scripted/cron invocation has no interactive toggle, and so no `abort_retry`
  either; the wait between attempts races the run's cancel token, so Ctrl-C/SIGTERM ends it at once with
  the closing error record kept) rather than propagating a transient failure straight out of the
  process; a retried attempt's streamed output follows a `[transient error, retrying …]` stderr notice.
  The ceiling counts retries **without progress**: both `run_turn` and `serve`'s loop reset it when a
  failed attempt still committed a step (`session.steps` advanced), so a long run that recovered from
  three blips doesn't die on the fourth — which is how a 165-step eval run lost its progress. (`serve`
  keeps a separate cumulative `retry_attempt` for lifecycle and `auto_retry_end`; the `auto_retry_start`
  frame's `attempt` is the stall count.) Rate limits are mostly not this layer's job: `agent_core`
  waits them out inside the turn under a time budget (`--retry-rate-limit-secs` /
  `AI_AGENT_RETRY_RATE_LIMIT_SECS`, default 300, `retry::rate_limit_policy`, see `agent_core`'s
  `rate_limit.rs`), announcing each wait as an `AgentEvent::Retry` (`run` text mode prints
  `[rate limited, retrying in Ns (attempt n): …]` to stderr; `--json` and `serve` stream the event). A
  transport retry inside the turn (a 5xx or connection failure before the first byte, a broken stream)
  is announced the same way, as `AgentEvent::Retry { rate_limited: false }` (`[stream error, retrying
  …]`), so no retry is silent. An
  error that spent that budget leads with `rate_limit::BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, which
  `is_retryable_whole_run` refuses, so the run fails rather than restarting the wait. `--retry-max-retries`/`--retry-base-delay-ms`
  (`AI_AGENT_RETRY_MAX_RETRIES`/`AI_AGENT_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS`) configure this whole-run layer
  (`retry::RunRetryPolicy::from_overrides`) as well as `agent_core::client`'s pre-connect/mid-stream
  layer; `max_backoff` has no override of its own for this layer, capping at the fixed
  `RUN_RETRY_MAX_BACKOFF` constant even with a custom base.
- **Stale-cwd detection** — `cwd_is_stale` compares a session's recorded `cwd` against reality: the
  directory no longer exists, or (since `switch_session`/`fork`/reattaching never change the process's
  actual working directory) it simply isn't where this process is running. Surfaced as `cwd_stale` on
  `ready`, `get_state`, `new_session`, `switch_session`, and `fork` — the points a client picks up a
  session — rather than silently letting the model's tools run against a mismatched or missing
  directory.
- **Tool set filtering** — `--tools`/`--exclude-tools`/`--no-tools` (both `run` and `serve`) restrict
  or drop from the constructed registry before it's advertised to the model; the auto-generated system
  prompt's tool list (`default_system_prompt`) reflects the filtered set, not the full constructed one, so a
  restricted agent never sees itself advertised a tool it doesn't actually have. A bare invocation
  advertises nine tools (`read`/`write`/`edit`/`bash`/`bash_job`/`ls`/`grep`/`find`/`todo`; `bash_job` is kept or dropped with `bash`). `web` stays
  constructed so `--tools web` can opt it in, but is **not** advertised by default (a TB polyglot run
  burned most of its `$` fetching pages). When `grep` and `read` are registered, the system prompt
  prefers those over bash for search and file contents. Do not `bash grep`/`rg`/`cat`/`sed`; if you
  must sample via bash, `| head` that grep/cat/ls only — never `| head`/`| tail` installs or tests
  (hides exit status; unbounded grep/cat overflowed the ~50KB bash cap, and bash keeps the tail).
  When that bullet does not fire but `bash` is registered (e.g. `--exclude-tools grep`), the pipe rule
  stands alone ("Never pipe installs or test runs through `| head`/`| tail`") instead of vanishing
  with it. Use read instead of cat (read paginates from the start). The `todo` protocol in the system prompt says only what
  the tool can't: use it for multi-step work, and move an item as you start and finish it. Full
  replacement, one `in_progress`, the field tenses and "empty clears" live on the tool's description
  and schema, said once.
- **Selection flags are checked at startup** (`tools/selection.rs`, `skills::check_paths`) — filter
  lists match names exactly, so a typo used to match nothing: `--tools raed,bash` ran without `read`,
  and a mistyped `--exclude-tools`/`--deny-tool` removed or blocked nothing. `run` and `serve` now
  refuse, before any model call, a name in `--tools`/`--exclude-tools`/`--deny-tool` that is neither a
  built-in (`selection::BUILTIN_TOOLS`, kept in step with the default registry by a test) nor an MCP
  name, and name the closest built-in (``--tools: unknown tool `raed` (did you mean `read`?)``). MCP
  tools exist only once their server connects, after this check, so any `mcp__…` name is accepted as
  is; every MCP tool is registered as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, so the prefix can't collide with a
  built-in. `--no-tools` with `--tools` or `--exclude-tools` is refused as contradictory. A `--skill`
  or `--prompt-template` path given on this invocation that is neither a directory nor a `.md` file
  is refused too (`--skill /nope/skill: does not exist`); before, discovery only recorded it as a
  diagnostic, which `run` never shows. Pattern entries (`!x`, globs) and stored default paths are left
  to discovery.
- **Code Mode** — `--code-mode` / `AI_AGENT_CODE_MODE` (both `run` and `serve`, off by default), and
  **not linked into the default binary**. Without it MCP tools load through `tool_search` or eagerly
  (see "Deferred MCP tools" for the measured comparison of all three). MCP tools stop being advertised as flattened
  `mcp__<server>__<tool>` entries and become a deferred catalog inside one `execute` tool
  ([`tools/code_mode.rs`](src/tools/code_mode.rs)). The model writes a small JavaScript program; a
  confined QuickJS-NG runtime (`rquickjs`, no module loader, no `os`/`std` host modules, no Date /
  Proxy / TypedArrays / MapSet) runs it against `tools.<server>.<method>(input)` Promises. Built-in
  coding tools stay direct. Nested calls honor `--exclude-tools` / `--deny-tool`. Budgets: 30s wall
  clock, 64 nested calls, 256 KiB result, **4 MiB JS heap**, **128 KiB JS stack**, and **one QuickJS
  runtime per process** (a `serve` daemon never holds two heaps at once). QuickJS evaluates synchronously, so evaluation runs on the blocking pool under a local executor, never on the runtime thread other sessions share: a spinning script holds a pool thread until its interrupt (deadline, cancellation, or the call being dropped — a guard trips it) fires, and the one-heap slot is released when the evaluation really ends. Nested host calls are spawned back onto the session's runtime, under the script's deadline (which so holds across a nested await, not only while JS runs), and aborted by the same guard however the run ends — cancelled or dropped — so no host tool runs on after it. An allow-list of built-ins
  (`--tools read,bash`) still keeps `execute` so the deferred catalog is reachable; `--exclude-tools
  execute` (or `--no-tools`) drops it. An empty deferred catalog (no MCP servers, or every MCP tool
  excluded or denied) registers no `execute` (`code_mode::execute_tool`): the JS context reaches
  nothing else, so it would be ~270 schema tokens per request for a tool that can do nothing. A
  registry rebuild (`set_model`, an MCP hot-plug) re-checks. Subagents inherit the parent's flag so a child cannot
  re-advertise the catalog the parent deferred. QuickJS is a cargo feature (`code-mode`) because idle
  RSS in a 768 MB guest is dominated by resident `.text` — linking the interpreter into every agent VM
  costs ~1 MB of code even when the operator never passes the flag (the same class of cost that
  rejected aws-lc). `--code-mode` on a density-default binary is a hard error, not a silent fallback.
  Release builds (`release-agent.yml`) must not enable the feature. Experiments:

  ```sh
  cargo run -p beyond-ai-agent --features code-mode -- run --code-mode …
  ```

  This is the OpenCode/Cloudflare "code mode" pattern aimed at MCP-heavy context and multi-hop
  composition — measure `$/pass`, turns, schema tokens, **and RSS / `.text`** before making it a
  default. [`tests/code_mode_eval.rs`](tests/code_mode_eval.rs) is a **smoke** (catalog-byte A/B + a
  scripted `execute` composition against the MCP fixture; live Grok 4.6 / OpenRouter is
  `#[ignore]`), not an eval. Density: [`tests/code_mode_density.rs`](tests/code_mode_density.rs)
  (default binary must not contain `JS_NewRuntime`). Harness eval is Harbor on a FrontierHarness
  v1.0 Terminal-Bench subset ([`eval/harbor_beyond_agent.py`](eval/harbor_beyond_agent.py),
  [`eval/run_frontier_subset.sh`](eval/run_frontier_subset.sh)) — verifier pass/fail and tokens.
  `$` is one OpenRouter list-price card applied to both arms
  ([`eval/tabulate_harbor_job.py`](eval/tabulate_harbor_job.py), [`eval/token_price.py`](eval/token_price.py));
  do not compare Harbor's raw `cost_usd` (Pi copies billed `usage.cost`, beyond fills list).
  Harbor `n_input_tokens` includes cache. Three arms, same tasks, same model
  (**GLM 5.3** / `z-ai/glm-5.3` by default; `MODEL=moonshotai/kimi-k3` for the
  published FrontierHarness freeze): `HARNESS=beyond` (density-default, no
  QuickJS), `HARNESS=beyond-code-mode` (`--features code-mode` binary + `--code-mode`), and
  `HARNESS=pi` (Harbor's Pi agent at FrontierHarness pin **0.84.2**). The shipped binary does
  not advertise `web` (a TB polyglot run burned most of its `$` fetching pages); `--tools web`
  opts it in. Do not disable thinking on the eval adapter to chase Pi: Harbor's Pi 0.84.2 pin
  also defaults to medium (`DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL`). GLM-5.3 always thinks
  (`z-ai/glm-5.3` on OpenRouter: nested `reasoning:{effort}`, `medium`→`high`;
  `thinking.disabled` is rejected). Kimi K3 is the same always-on class; omitting
  `reasoning_effort` selects the provider default `max`. A historical polyglot `$`
  gap after dropping `web` was a Kimi K3 catalog miss (treated as K2, provider-default
  `max`), not thinking-on vs thinking-off. Iterate by changing one thing and re-running
  the expensive task
  (`TASKS=terminal-bench/polyglot-c-py`). TB has no MCP catalog, so beyond vs Code Mode on that
  slice is a regression/overhead check (with no
  MCP catalog `execute` is not registered at all), not the MCP schema-token win. The Code Mode eval is
  `HARNESS=beyond-mcp` vs `HARNESS=beyond-mcp-code-mode`: local Harbor task
  [`eval/tasks/ast-hotspots`](eval/tasks/ast-hotspots) plus a stdlib Python AST MCP (`list_functions`,
  `find_calls`, …) — tree-sitter-shaped, no native parser, useful on a coding guest. Flattened
  `mcp__ast__*` vs `--code-mode` `execute`. Pi is the TB harness baseline. Code Mode still needs
  this MCP-heavy verifier (and RSS/`.text`) before it can be a default. The TB slice is not the
  published 30-task board (21 TB + 9 DeepSWE) and not a Runta golden-checkpoint run.

  The compaction-trigger eval is [`eval/longctx`](eval/longctx) (`mise run eval:longctx`). Its tasks
  are real Python repos at pinned tags with ~4–5K lines of function bodies cut back to
  `raise NotImplementedError` (Commit0-style; [`eval/longctx/specs`](eval/longctx/specs) pins which),
  two or three repos per workspace so a run's context passes 200K. The grade is each repo's own
  test suite with the pristine tests restored. A numeric arm (`100k`, `200k`, any `<n>k`) sets
  `--context-window` to trigger + 16,384 for older binaries and `AI_AGENT_COMPACT_AT` to the trigger
  for newer ones, so compaction fires at the arm's trigger on both; `default` sets
  `AI_AGENT_COMPACT_AT=0` (window − reserve, no per-model cap) and `model` leaves the binary's own
  per-model `compact_at` in place. Each result records its masking passes (`maskings`, `masking_log`
  from the `tool_output_masked` events) and the extra agent flags it ran with (`agent_args`). A mechanism
  A/B runs one commit against itself with the mechanism toggled on one side, e.g.
  `ab.py run --base X --cand X --base-arg=--no-tool-masking` or `--base-arg=--no-cached-summary`;
  `compaction_log` carries each summary call's `cr`/`cw`/`i`/`o` for the cache-read share. `$` is priced per request from the usage on the `run
  --json` stream, plus `Compacted.usage` for the summarization calls, which no `Stream(Usage)`
  event carries. `BASE=<sha> CAND=<sha> mise run eval:ab` reuses the same tasks as a
  before/after no-regression gate ([`eval/longctx/ab.py`](eval/longctx/ab.py)): both commits at
  one compaction arm (`--arm`, default `default`), `--base-arg`/`--cand-arg` adding agent flags to
  one side so a commit can be A/B'd against itself with one mechanism toggled, plus four prompt-prefix tasks (the one fact each needs sits where the skills,
  memory-index or context-file budget can cut it) and four MCP tasks run with Playwright, GitHub
  and filesystem servers configured, on the candidate both with tool search and with `--code-mode`.

  The code tasks' integrity guarantees, each checked by `mise run eval:validate` (local, no model
  calls), which must pass before an A/B is trusted:
  - **No answer key in reach.** A task tree is a clean copy of the pristine tree: no `__pycache__`,
    `.pyc`, `.so`, `.egg-info`/`.dist-info`, VCS dir, vendored install or patch file, and no removed
    body left verbatim elsewhere in the tree (boltons' vendored `OrderedMultiDict` copy and three
    other duplicates were dropped from the specs). `tasks.build` refuses a tree that breaks either
    rule, cached or fresh. The agent runs in [`sandbox.py`](eval/longctx/sandbox.py)'s user + mount +
    PID namespace: the work dir (pristine trees, built tasks, every other run), the repo and all of
    `/home` are empty read-only mounts with only the venv, its base interpreter (minus its
    site-packages), the agent binary and `rg` bound back; `/tmp` is private per run; a fresh
    `/proc`, `no_new_privs` and an unmapped host root close `/proc/<pid>/root`, sudo and the docker
    socket. The validator walks the agent's whole reachable filesystem for any copy of a package
    under test. The network stays open (the agent needs its provider); the prompt forbids fetching
    and `suspect` flags it.
  - **Graded in one place.** The workspace is `/tmp/longctx/work` in every run, arm and grade, so
    no test sees the host run dir (boltons' `test_iter_find_files` strips characters, not a prefix,
    and failed in every run dir containing an `f`, i.e. every `default` arm).
  - **The pristine tree passes 100%.** Tests that can't pass in this environment for reasons no
    reimplementation fixes are deselected for agent and grader alike (`Repo.deselect`: parso's 14
    interpreter-message checks, pyparsing's railroad-diagram example); marshmallow gets a
    metadata-only `dist-info` so `importlib.metadata.version` works as in upstream's installed test
    env. Test ids holding a clock time (`now()` parameters) collapse to one id, which passes only if
    every instance does; before that, two marshmallow ids could never match the baseline, so
    marshmallow could not pass. The validator grades the perfect answer through `run.grade` in four
    run-dir layouts and requires solved, identical results.
  - **Endings are recorded, not guessed.** Each result carries `end_reason` (`completed`,
    `max_steps`, `wall`, `cap`, `error`, `crash`), `cut_off`, `tree_state` (`ok`, `mid_edit` when a
    library file no longer parses, `suite_hang`, `no_report`) and, for a mid-edit tree,
    `last_parseable`: the grade of the last state in which every library file parsed, snapshotted
    after each tool call outside the agent's view. The reports split cut-off runs out.
  - **Errors the exit code hid.** `tool_errors` counts `is_error` results; `soft_errors` counts bash
    results showing a traceback or an `AssertionError`/`SyntaxError`/`IndentationError` line behind
    a zero exit (`pytest | tail`), each also marked `soft_error` on its `tool_end` event. Events
    carry `t` (seconds since start), each turn's text is logged as `assistant_text`, and the result
    keeps `final_text` and `started_at`.

  Eight background-process tasks ([`eval/longctx/bg_tasks.py`](eval/longctx/bg_tasks.py)) measure
  `bash` jobs, where the code tasks cannot (they have no server or watcher): generated stdlib repos
  whose work needs a process kept running — a server bug reproduced with curl, an API plus its worker
  over SQLite, a test watcher kept going, a 100 s build with other edits meanwhile, a dev server that
  invites "start it with `timeout_ms: 1000`", a configured port held by a squatter the agent cannot see
  or kill (it runs in the harness, outside the sandbox's PID namespace), an error only the server log
  shows under a load script, and an obligation to leave nothing running. Each `check` starts the
  agent's code afresh on ports of its own (never reads the transcript); every port is an flock-held
  lease below the ephemeral range, so parallel runs and both A/B arms never collide. The sandbox's
  init writes, once the agent exits and before the namespace dies, the processes still running
  (`sandbox.survivors`, by namespace membership, so the same for every build): the result's
  `processes_left`. Every sandboxed result also carries `bg` ([`bg_metrics.py`](eval/longctx/bg_metrics.py)):
  `run_in_background` and shell `&` uses, `timeout_ms` set/short/returns/kills, idle yields, seconds
  blocked in `bash_job` waits (`job_wait_s`), finish notices, end-of-run reminders, sleep-polls, launches and duplicate launches, jobs stopped at end.
  `ab.py report` prints them per arm and per task, and checks the pre-registered ship rule
  (`ab.SHIP_RULE`: background pass rate holds, median wall falls, no process left in any candidate run,
  the four code tasks lose no passes against `--code-baseline`). `validate.py --bg-only` sets all
  eight up at once and checks that each untouched task fails and its reference solution passes, three
  times each, plus ports, graders' processes, the real build's bundle, the leftover report and the
  metrics on a synthetic log; [`mock_model.py`](eval/longctx/mock_model.py) drives the real agent
  through every task's reference trajectory with a scripted Responses-API model on localhost (no
  credential in its environment), starting processes with `run_in_background` where `bash` has it and
  `nohup … &` where it does not.

  ```sh
  cargo test -p beyond-ai-agent --test code_mode_density
  cargo test -p beyond-ai-agent --features code-mode --test code_mode_eval -- --nocapture
  # live MCP smoke (bills a real request; not an eval):
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY=… cargo test -p beyond-ai-agent --features code-mode --test code_mode_eval -- --ignored --nocapture
  # Harbor TB subset (Docker; GLM 5.3 via OpenRouter; not the Kimi K3 FH board):
  cargo build -p beyond-ai-agent --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
  HARNESS=beyond JOBS_DIR=/tmp/beyond-frontier-beyond crates/agent/eval/run_frontier_subset.sh
  cargo build -p beyond-ai-agent --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --features code-mode
  cp target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/beyond-ai-agent \
    target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/beyond-ai-agent-code-mode
  HARNESS=beyond-code-mode JOBS_DIR=/tmp/beyond-frontier-code-mode crates/agent/eval/run_frontier_subset.sh
  HARNESS=pi JOBS_DIR=/tmp/beyond-frontier-pi crates/agent/eval/run_frontier_subset.sh
  # one-task loop vs Pi (example: the expensive polyglot):
  TASKS=terminal-bench/polyglot-c-py HARNESS=beyond JOBS_DIR=/tmp/poly-beyond \
    crates/agent/eval/run_frontier_subset.sh
  TASKS=terminal-bench/polyglot-c-py HARNESS=pi JOBS_DIR=/tmp/poly-pi \
    crates/agent/eval/run_frontier_subset.sh
  # Code Mode with a real MCP catalog (AST hotspots, hidden verifier):
  HARNESS=beyond-mcp JOBS_DIR=/tmp/ast-flat crates/agent/eval/run_frontier_subset.sh
  HARNESS=beyond-mcp-code-mode JOBS_DIR=/tmp/ast-code crates/agent/eval/run_frontier_subset.sh
  ```
- **Multimodal** — `prompt` accepts `images: [{media_type, data}]` (base64), built into a multimodal
  user turn. `read` on an oversized image file downscales/re-encodes it (Lanczos3, PNG-then-JPEG
  re-encode, Exif orientation correction via the `image` crate's own generic
  `ImageDecoder::orientation`/`DynamicImage::apply_orientation` — correct for every format that can
  carry Exif, JPEG and WebP included, with no per-format parser of our own to maintain) to fit a
  4.5 MB base64 budget rather than refusing outright, and sniffs the real magic bytes to recover from
  a mislabeled extension. Decode/resize/re-encode runs on `spawn_blocking` (same pattern as `grep`/
  `find`'s own blocking walks), not inline on the async runtime — CPU-bound work on a large image can
  take a while, and pi's own equivalent (`resizeImageInProcess`) runs its decode/resize/encode in a
  worker thread for the same reason: so it can't stall unrelated concurrent work. A resized image's text
  note states both dimension pairs _and_ the coordinate-scale multiplier (`orig_w / new_w` — the resize
  preserves aspect ratio, so either dimension's ratio agrees) needed to map a point identified in the
  downscaled image back to the original's coordinate space, matching pi's `formatDimensionNote` rather
  than leaving the model to re-derive (and potentially mis-derive) it.

---

## Where state lives — `~/.beyond`, and `~/.claude` read-only

Everything the agent writes about itself lives in **`~/.beyond`** (`settings::config_dir_root`), or
in `$AI_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR` when that is set (it names the directory itself):

| File                                          | What                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `settings.json`                               | `agent settings` defaults (global tier)                   |
| `auth.json`, `mcp_auth.json`                  | `agent login` and MCP OAuth credentials (0600)            |
| `trusted-projects.json`                       | `agent trust`/`untrust` grants                            |
| `models.json`                                 | per-model connection overrides (hand-edited)              |
| `projects/<encoded-cwd>/memory/`              | durable memory (`memory::file::FileBackend::for_project`) |
| `mcp-manifest.json`, `mcp-manifest-apps.json` | MCP tool-list cache (`ManifestDir::from_home`)            |
| `sessions/<encoded-cwd>/`                     | the default session repo (`session_store::sessions_root`) |

The task-journal key and every other per-session sidecar sit beside their session, so they follow the
session directory. `--session-dir`/`AI_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, `--memory` and the stored
`default_session_dir` still override their defaults. A project's own settings file is
`<cwd>/.beyond/settings.json`.

**`~/.claude` is Claude Code's directory, and the agent never writes under it.** It reads it as
compatibility input only: skills (`~/.claude/skills`), agent definitions (`~/.claude/agents`), prompt
templates (`~/.claude/prompts`), `CLAUDE.md`, `SYSTEM.md`/`APPEND_SYSTEM.md`, and in a project
`<cwd>/.claude/{skills,agents,prompts,SYSTEM.md,settings.json}` (trust-gated as before). A project's
`.claude/settings.json` contributes only the keys `Settings` models, below `.beyond/settings.json`.
The reason is ownership: Claude Code owns `~/.claude/settings.json` (permissions, hooks, env), and a
typed rewrite of it from here dropped every key this crate doesn't model; our session directories
were also mixed in with Claude Code's own `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` files, and our durable
memory shared Claude Code's per-project `~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/memory/` directory.

**A clean break, no migration.** Nothing reads the agent's old files from `~/.claude`. An existing
user runs `agent login` and `agent trust` again, re-applies any `agent settings` and copies
`models.json` across by hand if they had one; sessions under `~/.claude/sessions` are no longer
listed or resumable by id (a `.jsonl` path still opens with `--session <path>`), and old memory under
`~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/memory/` is no longer read. Claude Code's own per-project memory there is
not surfaced by the memory tool.

Proof: `tests/state_dir.rs` runs `settings`, `trust`, `auth-status`/`logout`, a session-creating `run`
and a full `mcp-login` with `HOME` pointed at a temp dir holding a stocked `~/.claude` (a Claude Code
`settings.json` with permissions, hooks and env, a legacy `auth.json`, a `sessions/<pid>.json`), and
asserts the whole `~/.claude` tree — paths, bytes, mtimes — is unchanged while the state lands in
`~/.beyond`.

## Data Flow

### `run` — one-shot CLI

```
beyond-ai-agent run "<task>"
   │
   ▼
expand_if_skill_invocation → expand_if_slash (same expansion `serve`'s "prompt" handler applies —
   │                          a `/skill:name` or `/name args` first message/arg is expanded before
   │                          the model ever sees it; project-local skills/templates gated by
   │                          `project_trusted` same as `serve`)
   ▼
Session::new() + user(expanded task)
   │
   ▼
Agent::run[_events] (agent_core loop; see agent-core/ARCHITECTURE.md for the loop itself)
   │  each step, text mode (default) — Agent::run, StreamEvent only:
   │   ├─ POST one model turn → gateway or provider ─── network/4xx/5xx ──► Error::Transport, exit ≠0
   │   ├─ StreamEvent::TextDelta   ───────────────────────────────────────► stdout (via TextOut)
   │   ├─ StreamEvent::ToolUseStart ──────────────────────────────────────► stdout "\n[tool: name]"
   │   ├─ TextOut: stdout not a TTY → a step's output is held until its TurnEnd, and a retried
   │   │   attempt's (AgentEvent::Retry, or a whole-run retry) is dropped, so a captured stdout is
   │   │   the answer, never PARTIAL-PARTIAL-ANSWER; stdout a TTY → printed live, and a retry writes
   │   │   "[attempt failed; the text above is discarded, retrying]" after the shown partial
   │   └─ assistant turn carries tool_use blocks → ToolRegistry.get(name)
   │        │
   │        ├─ found    → tool.run(input) → Ok(text) / Err(ToolError) ──► tool_result (is_error?)
   │        └─ not found → "unknown tool: <name>" ───────────────────────► tool_result, is_error=true
   │  each step, `--json` — Agent::run_events, the full AgentEvent surface (same shape `serve` streams):
   │   └─ every AgentEvent (AgentStart/TurnStart/Stream(..)/ToolStart/ToolProgress/ToolEnd/TurnEnd/
   │        Compacted/AgentEnd/Error) ──► stdout, one `serde_json::to_string`-d object per line, flushed
   │        immediately; a `{"kind":"session", id, model, cwd}` header line precedes the first event
   │
   │  every stdout write above (text or `--json`) goes through `write_stdout_or_exit` (Task #10
   │  pi-parity fix): on `ErrorKind::BrokenPipe` (a downstream consumer like `head -1` closing its
   │  read end) it calls `std::process::exit(0)` immediately instead of `println!`/`print!`'s own
   │  internal panic-on-write-error — a closed pipe is a normal way for a Unix producer's run to end
   │
   ▼ (model ends its turn without a tool_use, or hits an opted-in --max-steps ceiling)
stdout: trailing newline (text mode only — `--json` has no extra trailing line, just the event stream)
stderr: "[stopped at the --max-steps ceiling (N): …]" when the run reached its ceiling and ended on the
        model's wrap-up answer (`AgentEvent::WrapUp` seen, `RUN_WRAPPED_UP`). Still exit 0, on evidence:
        the wrap-up grant exists to turn a cut-off run into a usable answer (agent-core's "Wrap-up at
        the step ceiling"), a run that can't stop within it already fails with `MaxSteps`, and the
        eval harnesses read the `--json` events (longctx's `end_reason`) or treat a non-zero exit as
        a warning only (harbor), so a new code would buy nothing a stderr line doesn't; `--json`
        consumers already get the `wrap_up` event.
--export:  written however the run ends: success, a failed turn, a cancel (before `exit_cancelled`)
        or a closed stdout — a failed run's transcript is the one most worth reading.
stderr: "[done in N step(s); X in / Y out tokens]"   (or the propagated Error::MaxSteps / Error::Transport)
        text mode only: last turn's StopReason::Refusal ──► stderr "[refused]", exit(1) — matching
        pi's own print-mode text-mode behavior; `--json` already carries `stop_reason` on every
        `TurnEnd` event in its own stream, so its exit code stays reserved for a genuine process failure.
        `StopReason::Aborted` gets the identical treatment (stderr "[cancelled]", exit(1)) — see
        `text_mode_failure_message`'s own doc comment for why this is currently unreachable from
        `run_task` (every reachable cancellation path already exits earlier, via `unwrap_turn_result`'s
        `Err(Error::Cancelled)` handling, with the matching POSIX `128+signal` code — see below — when a
        real shutdown signal caused it, else `exit(1)`) but checked anyway, defensively
```

With `--session`/`--continue`, persistence is incremental, not just once at the end of each whole turn:
`main.rs`'s `DirectCheckpoint` (an `agent_core::CheckpointHook`, sharing the same `SessionStore` — behind
an `Arc<Mutex<Option<SessionStore>>>` since the hook only gets `&self` — that `persist_run` also
writes to after each `run_turn` call returns) durably appends every mid-run checkpoint (after each tool
round-trip) as it happens. **Every persist path, `run`'s and `serve`'s, goes through
`SessionStore::persist`, keyed on the compaction generation as well as the message count**: the store
remembers `Session::compaction` as of its last write (`written`, set from the session `open` returns),
and a session whose generation differs is written with `rewrite_compacted` first (its `tokens_before`
read back off the summary by `agent_core::compaction::summary_tokens_before`), then masked results, then
what is new. The generation is a claim the store checks: a compaction always puts a fresh summary at
`messages[0]` (the one message no in-memory-only rewrite — scrub, masking, MCP splice — touches), so a
generation that moved while the first message is still the stored one is a session rebuilt without the
store's provenance, and its count is adopted rather than taken for a compaction. `serve`'s
`switch_branch` hands back a session carrying `SessionStore::compaction_provenance` for the same reason:
it used to hand back `Session::new()`'s defaults, and the next persist read the reset generation as a
compaction. `rewrite_compacted` never falls back to a full rewrite: the folded messages are the stored
active path up to where the kept suffix (`messages[1..]`) begins, found by content, so a store that
lagged the session (failed checkpoints) still writes an append-only round, appending kept messages it
never had — the count-based fold read that as "nothing folded" and rewrote the file, dropping every
model change, label, title and earlier compaction record (`tests/session_compaction_continuity.rs`).
**A transcript cut back in place is rewound before the append.** Every in-place shrink goes through
`agent_core::Session::cut_back` (and an in-place rewrite of the tail through `rewriting_from`), which
records `(id, length)` in `Session::cuts`; `persist` takes the cuts newer than the last one it applied
(`cuts_seen`, starting at `agent_core::cut_watermark()` when the store opens, so a cut on a transcript
it never wrote is ignored), and when the shortest length is below what it wrote, moves the active tip
back with a `Leaf` to the last entry that length keeps, then appends. A list shorter than what is on
disk with no compaction behind it is rewound the same way, recorded or not. The silent-truncation
recovery is why: the agent pops the cut-off reply that the compaction's own checkpoint already wrote,
then pushes the retry, so the count comes back where it was and a count-keyed append wrote nothing — a
reopen got the cut-off reply, or a retried tool call's `tool_result` with no `tool_use` before it.
Content comparison is deliberately not the signal: the in-memory transcript legitimately differs from
disk in ways that must never be written back (a cross-model scrub). `serve`'s checkpoint carries the
cuts alongside the provenance and edits (`tests/session_retry_persist.rs`, through both binaries). `Agent::compact` checkpoints right after its rewrite, so the
compaction is on disk before anything else is appended. `append_new` alone is count-keyed and reads a
compaction's shrink as "nothing new": `run` used to skip every message after a compaction until the list
outgrew its old length, then chain the wrong tail onto the uncompacted history
(`run_compaction_persist`), and `serve`'s mid-run checkpoints did the same until the end-of-turn rewrite
corrected it, so a crash in between left a corrupt session and lost the compaction's provenance
(`serve_compaction_persist` kills the process in that window and reloads). `serve`'s checkpoint carries
the session's provenance for this; a manual `compact` resolves `first_kept_entry_id` against the active
path as it was before the compaction's own checkpoint rewrote it. `serve`'s `ChannelCheckpoint` forwards checkpoints through an `mpsc` channel instead of writing directly, because it needs to keep servicing concurrent stdin commands from a `select!` loop while a run is in flight — and **waits for the loop's acknowledgement that the write is on disk** before returning. The agent awaits a checkpoint before it dispatches a tool, so that wait is what makes "the `tool_use` is durable before the tool runs" true; a checkpoint that only queued the write let the tool start (and `tool_start` reach the client) first, and a crash in that window lost the record of the call — a load-only failure of `serve_session_lifecycle`'s crash test, now pinned with a slow-checkpoint seam (`BEYOND_AI_AGENT_TEST_SLOW_CHECKPOINT_MS`). Every path that drives the agent drains the channel while it waits: the prompt loop and a manual `compact` (whose closing checkpoint would otherwise wait forever); a snapshot swept undrained resolves its wait without a write; and the acknowledgement carries the write's result, sent only once the write is done. **A failed write fails closed**: before a tool dispatch the agent then runs no tool and ends the run with `Error::Checkpoint` ("the tool call could not be recorded durably, so it was not run"), which `serve` reports on the `prompt` response like any other persistence failure, and `run`'s `DirectCheckpoint` returns its append error the same way — a write that failed leaves the same hole as one that never happened. Checkpoints with no tool waiting stay best-effort (`serve_session_lifecycle`: `a_failed_checkpoint_before_a_tool_means_the_tool_never_runs`, `serve_reports_success_when_a_failed_checkpoint_is_superseded_by_a_successful_final_persist`); `run` has no such concurrent event source, so a direct blocking
append inside the async callback is the simpler correct choice here. Without this, a long multi-step
turn (several tool round-trips, each running a real command or editing a real file) that crashed or hard-
failed partway through left _no session record at all_ of the round-trips that had already happened —
`persist_run` runs after every `run_turn` call regardless of outcome (`Ok` or `Err`, including a
`Cancelled` shutdown-signal stop — see below), not just on success, so a cancelled or errored turn's own
tail (its final, possibly-partial assistant message) is never lost either. `serve`'s own `persist_error`
(the RunningTurn→Ready transition row above) reflects only the _final_ post-attempt persist's own
outcome — a mid-run checkpoint's failure is logged, not tracked, since that final persist re-persists the
whole session fresh regardless and so is a strict superset of every checkpoint along the way; a
checkpoint hiccup superseded by a successful final write must not surface as a false failure.

`run_task`'s `Agent` also carries `.with_cache_key(meta.id.clone())` — the same prompt-cache affinity
key `serve`'s `build_agent` pins from `persistence.session_id()`. `meta` (via `fresh_meta`, or the
reopened session's own recorded id) is always in scope by the time the `Agent` is built, even for a
plain no-flag ephemeral run, so this costs nothing to always set. Without it, every turn of a `run`
invocation — including each sequential positional-message turn in one process, and every `--continue`
reattachment — picked no stable `x-client-request-id` session-affinity header at all (`client.rs`).
The session id also picks the session's routing bucket for the native OpenAI `prompt_cache_key` and
is that key outright on Codex and Copilot. Otherwise the key is a hash of the prefix, so sessions
with the same setup share a cache. See `agent-core/ARCHITECTURE.md`, "Why the Responses
`prompt_cache_key` is a hash of the prefix, not the session id".

**Deliberate divergence, awareness-only (pi-parity, not to be "fixed" toward pi's behavior): a session's
file/header is created and fsync'd immediately — `SessionStore::create` (`session_store.rs`), called from
`serve`'s startup (`Persistence::open`) and `run`'s `--session`/`--continue` paths, both before a single
prompt is composed or sent.** pi's own `SessionManager` defers this: `newSession()` only computes a path
and buffers entries in memory; the actual file write is gated on `_persist()` finding an assistant message
already present, so a session that never gets a reply (the user Ctrl-C's before the model responds) is
never written to disk at all — a deliberate anti-clutter choice (a regression test in pi's own suite
pins it: `tree-traversal.test.ts`, "the file should not exist yet... matching `newSession()` contract").
Beyond does the opposite on purpose, for a reason `DirectCheckpoint`'s own doc comment above states
directly: this agent's tool calls have _real_ side effects (a `bash` command, an `edit`/`write`), and a
crash mid-first-turn — after several of those already ran — must still leave a durable record of what
actually happened, not silently forget it the way pi's model would. Eagerly creating the file (still
empty of messages) is what makes the incremental mid-turn checkpointing described above possible at all;
deferring creation until an assistant reply exists would mean the _first_ turn's tool calls have nowhere
to be checkpointed to, reopening exactly the data-loss gap the checkpoint mechanism exists to close. The
one real cost is cosmetic: a session abandoned before its first reply leaves a near-empty (header-only,
zero-message) file behind, visible in `list_sessions`/`list_all_sessions` with `message_count: 0`. Judged
worth it — durability for real side-effecting tool calls over a tidier session list.

`run` also installs `serve`'s own `ShutdownSignal` (SIGTERM, SIGHUP, or SIGINT/Ctrl-C — SIGHUP's own
default disposition is the same immediate termination as an unhandled SIGTERM, so a controlling terminal
closing on a backgrounded `serve`/`run` needs the identical handling; matches pi's own `rpc-mode.ts`,
which treats SIGHUP the same as SIGTERM) — a shutdown request ties
into the _same_ `CancellationToken` `agent_core::Agent::run[_events]_cancellable` already drops tool
futures through on an explicit `abort`, so a `Ctrl-C`/`systemctl stop`/pod eviction mid-turn takes the
identical clean-cancellation path instead of Rust's default disposition (immediate termination, no
destructors run — a bash tool's `GroupKillGuard` never gets to `Drop` and reap a still-running child's
process group). `run_turn`/`run_turn_once` take the token by reference and pass a clone into
`run_events_cancellable`/`run_cancellable`; `Error::Cancelled` is deliberately excluded from both retry
layers (`is_retryable_mid_stream`/`is_retryable_whole_run`), so a shutdown request is never retried away.
A cancelled turn prints a clean `[cancelled]` (matching the `[refused]` precedent above) and exits —
Task #41 (pi-parity fix): `ShutdownSignal::wait` now returns _which_ signal actually fired
(`serve::Signal::{Term,Hup,Int}`), recorded into a `run_task`-local `Arc<Mutex<Option<Signal>>>`
(genuinely shared across a task boundary — the signal wait runs on its own spawned task — unlike
`serve()`'s own equivalent tracking, a bare local since every `shutdown.wait()` site there lives in one
async fn body) the spawned signal-waiting task writes to right before cancelling; `unwrap_turn_result`
reads it to exit with the matching POSIX `128+signal` code (143/129/130 for SIGTERM/SIGHUP/Ctrl-C — see
`Signal::exit_code`, matching pi's own `rpc-mode.ts`/`print-mode.ts`'s 143/129 for SIGTERM/SIGHUP,
extended to Ctrl-C for consistency since this crate already treats it as an equal graceful-shutdown
trigger) rather than the same undifferentiated `exit(1)` every cancellation used to get regardless of
cause — not a raw `Error: Cancelled` `Debug` dump of the bare enum variant either way. `serve` gets the
identical treatment: `serve()`'s own return type changed from bare `Result<(), _>` to
`Result<Option<Signal>, _>`, and `main.rs`'s `Command::Serve` arm exits with `shutdown_cause.map(
Signal::exit_code).unwrap_or(0)` instead of an unconditional `exit(0)`.

**A failed command prints one plain line.** `main` no longer returns its error to Rust's runtime,
which prints the `Debug` form (`Error: Os { code: 13, kind: PermissionDenied, .. }`,
`Transport("…")` with escaped quotes). `report_error` prints `error: <Display>` with the source chain
appended (unless the message already includes it) and exits 1, for every subcommand. Errors that
come from a path say which one: `SessionRepo::open_with` and the single-file create wrap the
`io::Error` as `cannot create session directory <path>: <os message>`, keeping its kind. The `--model`
help writes `{DEFAULT_MODEL}`, and `render_help` fills in the `DEFAULT_MODEL` constant whenever help
is printed, so the help can't name a different default from the one the code uses.

**Hints name the real command.** The binary is `beyond-ai-agent`, and every error, warning or
hint that tells a user what to run formats `beyond_ai_agent::PROGRAM` (the package name) in:
`` run `beyond-ai-agent login anthropic` ``, never a hard-coded `agent login`. Help text writes
`{PROGRAM}`, which `render_help` fills in. `program_name_tests.rs` scans the crate's string literals
for a command line spelled with another name, and a `main.rs` test checks every rendered help page.

The first signal is a request; a **second signal** is an order. `run`'s signal task keeps waiting after
it cancels, and a second SIGTERM/SIGHUP/Ctrl-C calls `exit_process` with that signal's code (the usual
exit cleanup still runs: job group kills, the stdio-server sweep), with `[second signal: exiting now]`
on stderr. The cooperative path covers everything that watches the token, including `--continue`'s MCP
task resume (`resume_mcp_tasks_for_run` selects each `resume_task` against `cancel`, and a cancelled
resume exits via `exit_cancelled` before any turn exists, leaving the task journaled); the second
signal covers a wait that doesn't, such as a hung MCP skill fetch while `/skill:server:name` expands.

### `serve` — headless NDJSON control protocol

```
stdin (one JSON command per line)              stdout (one JSON frame per line, single writer task)
  │                                                   ▲
  ▼                                                   │
serve() boot: open persistence (file/dir/none)        │
  │            + build static system prompt            │
  ▼                                                    ├── {"type":"ready", session_id, model, cwd_stale}
loop over stdin lines ──────────────────────────────► │
  │                                                    │
  ├─ {"type":"prompt", message, streaming_behavior?} ─► {"type":"ack", command:"prompt"}   (immediate)
  │     agent.set_system(static + fresh dynamic footer)
  │     session.user(message)                          event* (Stream / ToolStart / ToolProgress /
  │     Agent::run_events_steered(session, sink, ..)             ToolEnd / TurnEnd / Steered)
  │     persist (rewrite/rewrite_compacted as needed)   response{command:"prompt", success,
  │                                                              data:{steps, tokens…, refused: bool}}
  │     (busy + streaming_behavior set → queued via Steering, acked, no ack/event/response above)
  │
  ├─ {"type":"get_state"} ───────────────────────────► response{data:{session_id, model, steps,
  │                                                              message_count, input/output_tokens,
  │                                                              cwd, git_branch, thinking_level,
  │                                                              auto_compaction, auto_retry,
  │                                                              steering_mode, follow_up_mode,
  │                                                              pending_messages, session_file,
  │                                                              is_streaming, is_compacting}}
  ├─ {"type":"get_messages", since?} / {"type":"get_tree"} ──► response{data:{messages:[...]}} /
  │     (since: only what's new)                                 response{data:{nodes:[TreeNode…]}}
  ├─ {"type":"new_session"} ─────────────────────────► response{data:{session_id, parent}}  (fresh
  │     steering.clear()                                        Session; persisted per the open mode;
  │                                                              `parent` — repo mode only — is the
  │                                                              lineage marker below)
  ├─ {"type":"bash", command, cwd?, timeout_ms?} ─────► tool_progress*/tool_end event frames, then
  │     waits for exit; `timeout_ms` = the client's           response{command:"bash", success, data}
  │     deadline, enforced as a cancel
  ├─ {"type":"set_mcp_enabled", servers?} ───────────► response{data:{mode, enabled, configured}}
  │     omit/`null` = all configured; `[]` = none;               rebuilds the Agent so the next turn
  │     `["a","b"]` = allowlist (unknown names error)            advertises only the enabled MCP tools
  ├─ {"type":"get_mcp"} ─────────────────────────────► response{data:{mode, enabled, configured, tools,
  │                                                              resources, prompts, servers, apps}}
  ├─ {"type":"set_mcp_apps", enabled, mime_types?} ──► response{data:{enabled, mime_types, spec,
  │     this session's client renders MCP Apps                   servers, failed}}  (see "MCP Apps";
  │                                                              rebuilds the Agent like set_mcp_enabled;
  │                                                              a withdrawn declaration answers
  │                                                              success:false "superseded")
  │       ◄── unsolicited mcp_app_open{app_id, server, tool, resource, input} while a view-bearing
  │           tool runs, then mcp_app_result{app_id, server, result | cancelled{reason}}; both
  │           replayed (`replay: true`) to a connection that attaches later — a view of the turn
  │           in flight right after its own tool_start;
  │           mcp_app_teardown{app_id, server, reason} when the view is closed
  ├─ {"type":"mcp_app_request", server, app_id,   ───► response{data:{result}}  (a view's own
  │     request:{method, params}}                                tools/call, resources/read, ping,
  │     accepted busy or idle                                    notifications/message,
  │                                                              ui/update-model-context); a
  │                                                              tools/call may first raise an
  │                                                              approval_request (origin.app);
  │                                                              app_id must name an opened view
  ├─ {"type":"mcp_complete", server, ref, argument} ─► response{data:{completion}}  (MCP
  │                                                              `completion/complete` for prompt/resource
  │                                                              argument autocomplete — UI concern)
  ├─ {"type":"elicit", request_id, action, content?} ► resolves a pending MCP `elicitation/create`
  │                                                              (accept/decline/cancel); pairs with
  │                                                              unsolicited `elicitation_request` /
  │                                                              `elicitation_resolved` frames
  ├─ (idle; a `bash` job ends) ─────────────────────► event{kind:"background", reason:"finished",
  │     the session wakes: the notice becomes the               wake:true, text}, then a normal turn:
  │     input of a synthetic `prompt`                            ack, events, response{command:"prompt"}
  ├─ {"type":"mcp_events_subscribe"|"mcp_events_unsubscribe"|"mcp_events_list", …} ► response; pairs
  │                                                              with unsolicited `mcp_event` /
  │                                                              `mcp_event_status` frames (see
  │                                                              "MCP Events (draft extension)")
  └─ invalid JSON / unknown "type" ──────────────────► response{success:false, error}

See `serve.rs`'s own module doc for the full command list (session/branch nav, model/thinking/
auto-compaction tuning, skill/prompt discovery, `reload`, `abort`/`abort_bash`) — this diagram shows
the shape, not every command.

stdin EOF  →  out_tx dropped → writer drains queued frames → process exits Ok(())
stdout write fails (broken pipe) → writer task exits its loop → next emit! observes a closed
                                     channel → main loop breaks → process exits Ok(())
```

A `prompt`'s tool calls are NOT shown above as a separate fan-out: `agent_core::Agent::run_events_steered`
runs the tools the model batched in one turn **concurrently but bounded** (grouped by write-target so
same-path calls serialize, then `buffer_unordered` over ≤8 groups — see `agent-core/ARCHITECTURE.md`),
emits `ToolStart` for all of them up front (call order), then streams each call's own `ToolProgress`/
`ToolEnd` the instant it's known — a client sees completions in actual finish order, not batched after
the slowest call in the group — while the _persisted transcript_ is still rebuilt in call order
afterward, so on-disk determinism is unaffected by which tool actually finished first. Same-path write
exclusivity extends across the whole `serve` process via `write_locks: Arc<WriteLockRegistry>`, shared
by every `build_agent` rebuild (`set_model`/`set_thinking`/`cycle_model`/`cycle_thinking_level`/
`set_auto_compaction`/`set_auto_retry`) — not just re-derived per `Agent`.

**Intended `bash` jobs outlive the run in `serve`.** The session's job table lives on its `ExecCell`
(`EndPolicy::KeepRunning`), so ending a turn leaves intended jobs (`cmd &`) running and a `set_model`
rebuild keeps them; yielded ones (a foreground command that went quiet) are stopped as the prompt ends
(`BashJobs::end_turn`, on the blocking pool), reported in a `bash_jobs_stopped` frame before the
terminal `prompt` response.
When one ends while the session is idle, the idle loop's last `select!` arm (`bash_job_notice_due`)
fires: it waits `BASH_JOBS_WAKE_SETTLE` (200 ms, so jobs that end together fold into one turn), takes
the notices, emits a `background` event with `wake: true`, and feeds `{"type":"prompt", message:
<notice>, "bash_jobs_wake": true}` through the ordinary `prompt` path — persisted, streamed, retried like
any turn. The wait is level-triggered (a `watch` generation marked seen before the table is checked),
so a job that ends while the session is busy is never missed. A client prompt that races it wins (the
arm is last in a biased `select!`): its run delivers the notice at its first tool results or its stop,
and the arm then finds nothing to take, so no second turn runs. A transcript switch (`new_session`,
`switch_session`, `fork`, …) stops the jobs — they belong to the old history — on the blocking pool,
reported in a `bash_jobs_stopped` frame. The check is keyed on
`Persistence::transcript`, a counter every transcript-replacing command bumps, not on the session id:
a pinned session (every daemon session) and a `--session-file` session keep their id across
`new_session`, and the blank transcript must not wake about a job it never ran. The session's own
end (stdin EOF, the daemon's reaper, a closed socket, a supersede) stops them explicitly
(`BashJobs::stop_all` on the blocking pool as `serve_session` returns, reported in a
`bash_jobs_stopped` frame), so in a daemon, whose process lives on, nothing outlives its session. The
table is kept out of what the cell's runner and backend clone (`CellRoute`): every running job's task
holds the runner, and a runner that held the table would be a cycle that kept an ended session's jobs
alive, unreachable. Jobs do not survive a restart (or a reap, a deploy, a transcript switch); the
first run after one is told which jobs the transcript left running were stopped, and new jobs are
numbered past every id it used (see "Reopen" under "`bash` jobs"). `bash_job` on an id from before
one says it no longer exists.

a repo can hold many on disk | **`Steering`**                 | The two-lane queue (`steer`/`follow_up`) a client injects mid-run or at a stop boundary, plus a graceful stop-request flag (`request_stop`/`stop_after_turn`); persistent across a whole `serve` process, not just one `prompt` call. `pending_count` is a bare depth; `steer_texts`/`follow_up_texts` (Fix 5, pi-parity gap) are each lane's actual queued message text — a peek, not a drain — surfaced via `get_state`'s `steer_queue`/`follow_up_queue` and the `steer`/`follow_up` handlers' own ack `data`, not a separate unsolicited push-time event (that gap is deliberate — see `steering.rs`'s own module doc comment)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Not drained on a refusal (a distinct terminal condition) — queues cleared only on `new_session`/`switch_session`/`fork`/`switch_branch`;
